breadcrumb: 01. University of Oregon Institute for Policy Research & Engagement
tldr: The University of Oregon Institute for Policy Research & Engagement analyzes Oregon's fragmented economic development ecosystem (850+ organizations) against case studies from Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan, Colorado, and Kentucky. It advocates for Oregon to adopt a centralized/hierarchical model with gubernatorial leadership and Business Oregon as coordinating hub, establishing statewide priorities, measurable outcomes, formal regional structures, and integration with workforce and housing systems—mirroring successful approaches in the case study states.

bullets.text: Oregon's economic development ecosystem comprises more than 850 organizations operating within a decentralized/networked model without unified statewide strategy or shared outcomes
Primary recommendation: transition to centralized/hierarchical + public sector driven structure led by Governor with Business Oregon as the coordinating agency and implementation hub
All five case study states maintain clear state-level leadership with a central agency (DCED, ESD, MEDC, OEDIT, KCED) paired with formalized regional implementation structures
Economic development should be formally recognized as a fourth state priority pillar alongside housing, education, and behavioral health
Case study regional frameworks: New York has ten Regional Economic Development Councils; Kentucky has 15 Area Development Districts; Michigan has 14 planning regions

Successful states integrate economic development with workforce, housing, and infrastructure; Michigan's place-based revitalization coordinates land use, education, and business development in distressed areas
Oregon lacks shared planning capacity and technical resources in rural regions; states like Kentucky and Colorado invested in regional planning infrastructure to support under-resourced areas
Oregon's Equitable Economic Recovery Plan outlined six strategic imperatives but did not result in a fully coordinated statewide framework and remains one of several disconnected efforts
